items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And so I played fills behind her and Michael Masser he kept wanting, “Oh well let’s do one more, do one more.”

ctx.x: Were there sessions where you left after playing multiple solos and you didn’t know what they were going to use and you might not find out what they were going to use until you were in your car listening?

Every one, where I did multiple solos. I never knew what they were going to use. You’ve reminded me of a gentleman named Michael Masser. I can’t remember whether he’s still with us or not but he was a songwriter and record producer who called me one time, I didn’t know him but he got my number and said, “Listen I’m producing a new young lady. I think she’s a fantastic singer, I think she’s going to be a big star. Her name is Whitney Houston. And I’ve written a bunch of songs for her and I’d like you to play on…

You played on my record.” And I had to think a minute. “Oh yeah, yeah, right, hi, yes, how are you?” And she said, “I just wanted you to know that I really really loved the work you did on my record.” And I said, “Well thank you, how nice of you to call, thanks for taking the time to do that.” That was about the end of the conversation. And you know with all the things that happened to Whitney Houston since then, unfortunate things, tragic things obviously, I’ve always — whenever I hear anything said about her…
